free_tier.stated: certificates from the Public CA ACME endpoint are free; the quota is 100 new orders per hour per Google Cloud project, with wildcard names over the DNS challenge

per_object_cap.stated: no certificate size cap stated on the pages read; the quotas are on requests and not on objects

retention.stated: certificates are good for up to 90 days by default and a client may ask for as little as 1 day; the ACME account has no expiry, and an EAB secret must be used within 7 days

interface_detail: ACME v2 at https://dv.acme-v02.api.pki.goog/directory (staging at https://dv.acme-v02.test-api.pki.goog/directory) with external account binding required; the EAB key is made with the Public CA API or gcloud publicca external-account-keys create
tooling: certbot, acme.sh, any ACME client that supports EAB, the gcloud CLI for the EAB key
chaining: a free ACME CA run by a different operator than Let's Encrypt and ZeroSSL, with wildcard names over DNS-01 and certificates down to 1 day; the cost is a Google Cloud project that must be linked to a Cloud Billing account

limits.value: 100 new orders per hour per Google Cloud project, shared by all ACME accounts in that project
25 new accounts per minute and 100 per hour
an EAB secret is valid 7 days and registers one ACME account only
certificates are good for up to 90 days

binding_note: 100 new orders per hour per project bounds issuance, far above one user's need; the billing link on the project is the gate that decides who can use it

identity_cost.detail: a Google Cloud project is required, and the Cloud Billing page says a project not linked to an active Cloud Billing account cannot use Google Cloud services even when they are free; that account is tied to a Google payments profile and a payment method; the Public CA tutorial lists no billing step, so whether the Public CA API can be enabled with no payment method on file is unverified: behind a sign-up (https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/create-billing-account, https://docs.cloud.google.com/ruby/docs/reference/google-cloud-security-public_ca/latest)

reliability_note: the ACME service does not support retrying a challenge, so a client requests a new authorization after a failed validation; no outage history was read
confidence_note: the Public CA tutorial, concepts page, quota page, Google blog and ACME divergence page were captured and quoted; the production directory answered 200 with externalAccountRequired true. The card requirement is read from the billing page and a client-library quick start and was not seen at a sign-up.
